_meta.title: ARDF consolidated project policy, calibration, analysis, dashboard, and source manifest
_meta.architecture: one canonical evidence ledger + one policy file + one calibration/build script + one dashboard + four human-facing documents
_meta.note: This file consolidates the former calibration-algorithms.json, analysis-policy.json, dashboard-views.json, source-acquisition-manifest.json, and source-ledger.json.
refinements: policy top_end diagnostic corrected to direct task cost
source_version normalized to 7.3-refined for standardized proxy
empty models.dev fields documented as unavailable (not silently missing)
thin-evidence models (<8 pts) flagged with augmentation scaffold
validation added for embedded dashboard (no external generated/ dependency)

cost.comment: Every cost source is calibrated to task-level USD. Full-suite and source-specific costs remain raw evidence and are bridged through exact model overlaps.

algorithms.label: Robust affine (Theil-Sen)
algorithms.description: Median pairwise slope plus median intercept. Robust to outlying anchor models and the default production mapping. Cost is fitted in log10 space.

algorithms.label: Huber affine IRLS
algorithms.description: Weighted least squares with iterative Huber residual weights. More efficient than Theil-Sen when most anchors are clean, while limiting the leverage of outliers.

algorithms.label: Monotone piecewise linear
algorithms.description: Pools non-monotone anchor blocks with weighted isotonic regression, then linearly interpolates between anchor knots. Useful when benchmark scales compress or stretch nonlinearly.

algorithms.label: Auto-best per-group (lowest RMSE)
algorithms.description: Per calibration group picks the fitted mapping (robust, huber, or monotone) with lowest in-sample RMSE. Frontier from this column is the optimistic envelope; robust remains the conservative default.

identity_matching.comment: Exact model_key matching is required. calibration_group permits the same benchmark/version to share anchors across publishers while preserving source provenance.

task_cost_estimator.comment: This is a fallback coordinate, not a measured bill. The raw estimate is input tokens × input price + output/reasoning-equivalent tokens × output price. Multipoint calibration then maps the proxy to AA cost per task. Direct task-cost evidence outranks it in the dashboard.

token_price_proxy.source_label: AA token count × current blended token price proxy v7
token_price_proxy.comment: Uses model-specific AA evaluation token totals and the attached AA 7:2 blended token price. It is calibrated to task-level cost through exact overlaps with published AA cost-per-task records.

capability_tiers.label: Frontier ceiling
capability_tiers.note: Only ceiling: Opus 5 xhigh/max, Sol max

capability_tiers.label: Executor
capability_tiers.note: Strong executor 47-56, GLM-5.2 51.39 anchor; differentiated within tier by context/reasoning/tool/cache/provider

capability_tiers.label: Utility — bottom-4 interchangeable
capability_tiers.note: glm / deepseek / luna / muse variants within 0.5-2 cap for 2-4× cost are interchangeable on plane; choose by use-case matrix (context, reasoning, tool-call, cache)

executor.rationale: Rank every current priced configuration with positive calibrated capability by task cost divided by calibrated capability. Lower is better. Also report capability per dollar and cost per exact AA point when available. No global capability floor, capability subtraction, exponent, or hand-inserted candidate is applied. A named role or user question may apply its own visible capability gate outside this global value ranking.

top_end.primary_plane: multi-source calibrated capability vs operational task cost
top_end.same_source_diagnostic: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index vs direct Cost per Intelligence Index Task (full-evaluation cost as fallback when direct not published)
top_end.same_source_reason: Direct AA cost/task is primary; full-evaluation cost only fallback. This matches build-analysis.py and README v7.3. Previous value incorrectly said full cost only.
top_end.prune_rule: A configuration is sub-optimal on a plane if another configuration has <= cost and >= capability, with at least one strict inequality.

external_frontiers.x: AA cost per Intelligence Index task
external_frontiers.role: closest independent analogue to ARDF primary plane

dashboard.$comment: One entry is retained for every cataloged model/reasoning configuration. Paired points use precomputed calibration fields; incomplete configurations are rendered on labeled shelves rather than deleted by an inner join.

graph.x: USD per standardized task, token use multiplied by token price and calibrated
graph.incomplete_policy: display in labeled unpriced and unscored shelves
graph.calibration_location: calibrate.py; dashboard selects among precomputed calibration algorithms but never fits mappings

tables.record_grain: one card per exact release-dated models.dev canonical model
one row per canonical model_key after current filters
all currently selected atomic observations for one model_key

dashboard.frontier_rule: Among currently visible paired configuration points, sort by ascending task cost and retain a point only when its capability is strictly greater than every cheaper retained point. No fitted or smoothed curve is used.

current_sources.acquisition_used: Server-rendered benchmark-table extraction, with BenchLM mirror pages used during the original v5 import.
current_sources.preferred_acquisition: Start at the live Vals benchmark directory, open the exact benchmark detail page, extract every displayed model row, rank, score, update date and mode/harness label, and save the page/JSON payload as a dated raw snapshot.
current_sources.available_data: Model score, rank, benchmark update date, model count and benchmark description. The directory exposes many additional current benchmarks.
current_sources.unused_data: The current live page has more models and recent releases. Per-dimension app quality, task details, artifacts or rubric breakdowns may be available on the detail page/platform.
current_sources.caveats: The v7 snapshots are dated July 22–23 while the live Vals directory now shows August updates. Refresh them. Do not double-count Vals mirrors of official benchmarks alongside the official leaderboard without a correlation/down-weighting rule.
current_sources.automation: HTML table extraction; inspect network payload if stable

future_sources.name: SWE-bench official leaderboards and experiment records
future_sources.acquisition: Read data/leaderboards.json for the rendered leaderboard and ingest submission directories from the experiments repository for predictions, results, logs and trajectories.
future_sources.likely_findings: Verified/Lite/Multimodal scores, exact agent scaffold and submission date, trajectories, execution logs, model/provider labels and reproducibility metadata.
future_sources.value: Canonical coding-agent source; resolves ambiguity introduced by Vals/BenchLM mirrors and lets the project distinguish model from scaffold.

future_sources.name: Terminal-Bench official leaderboard and registry
future_sources.acquisition: Use the official leaderboard/registry data or scrape the versioned benchmark page. Record benchmark version, agent harness, environment image and task registry commit.
future_sources.likely_findings: Terminal-Bench 2.1/2.0 success, task-level results, model-agent combinations, registry metadata and challenge-specific evidence.
future_sources.value: Independent source for one of the most influential agentic metrics already appearing in vendor tables.

future_sources.name: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL V4)
future_sources.acquisition: Parse the official leaderboard or repository result artifacts at the pinned evaluation commit/package version.
future_sources.likely_findings: Overall and subcategory tool-use accuracy, agentic/multi-turn/live/non-live/hallucination scores, estimated total benchmark cost, latency, function-calling mode and format sensitivity.
future_sources.value: Rare source that provides capability, benchmark-wide USD cost and latency together, ideal for direct Pareto evidence.

future_sources.name: Aider Polyglot coding leaderboard
future_sources.acquisition: Scrape the official leaderboard table and preserve command/model string, effort, edit format and benchmark version.
future_sources.likely_findings: Percent correct, total benchmark cost, correct-edit-format rate, edit format and exact invocation command.
future_sources.value: Another direct capability-plus-cost source, with transparent coding workflow configuration.

future_sources.name: LiveCodeBench official leaderboard
future_sources.acquisition: Use official repository result files or the rendered leaderboard. Pin release_v1/release_v2, date window, scenario and fast/full setting.
future_sources.likely_findings: Pass@1 by difficulty, code generation, self-repair, execution and output-prediction scenarios, time-window freshness and model configuration.
future_sources.value: Contamination-limited coding evidence that complements SWE-bench’s repository repair focus.

future_sources.name: Epoch AI Benchmarking database
future_sources.acquisition: Download the official CSV or use the epochai Python client/Airtable API. Preserve whether each value was evaluated by Epoch or collected from an external official source.
future_sources.likely_findings: Many benchmark/model pairs, evaluation setup, repeats, source provenance, model release metadata and confidence/strict-scoring context.
future_sources.value: High-quality normalization layer with explicit provenance and downloadable structured data.

future_sources.name: Arena / LMArena leaderboard dataset
future_sources.acquisition: Load the official Hugging Face Parquet dataset rather than scraping the UI. Pin methodology/changelog version and arena type.
future_sources.likely_findings: Human-preference ratings, confidence intervals, sample counts, category/style controls, text/vision/agent arenas and historical snapshots.
future_sources.value: Adds human preference and confidence intervals, a useful orthogonal signal to automatic task benchmarks.

future_sources.name: OpenRouter Models and provider-performance API
future_sources.acquisition: Call the public models API; optionally query provider/model performance and generation records with authenticated access.
future_sources.likely_findings: Model/provider availability, exact routing IDs, pricing structures, context, architecture, supported parameters, creation date, recent throughput/latency and popularity/token-volume sorting.
future_sources.value: Best provider-routing and live-market complement to models.dev. Avoid using its AA-derived intelligence field as a new independent benchmark.

future_sources.name: Stanford HELM Capabilities
future_sources.acquisition: Use HELM result artifacts/framework outputs for a pinned leaderboard version, not screenshots.
future_sources.likely_findings: Scenario-level accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, efficiency and full prompt-level transparency under reproducible settings.
future_sources.value: Broad reproducible academic evidence and detailed prompt-level auditability.

future_sources.name: OSWorld / OSWorld 2.0 official results
future_sources.acquisition: Ingest official team-verified result tables and trajectory links. Record OSWorld version, agent scaffold, step budget and tool mode.
future_sources.likely_findings: Computer-use completion, partial score, model-agent configuration, verified trajectories, step/tool-call counts and safety reports.
future_sources.value: Adds genuine GUI/computer-use evidence for models whose marketing tables currently dominate that domain.

future_sources.name: BigCodeBench official leaderboard
future_sources.acquisition: Use official leaderboard data or evaluation-harness outputs, pin Full/Hard, Complete/Instruct and version.
future_sources.likely_findings: Pass@1 for practical multi-library code generation, hard/full subsets, instruction variants, model size and evaluation timing metadata.
future_sources.value: Broadens coding beyond repository patching into complex API/library use.

future_sources.name: METR time-horizon evaluations
future_sources.acquisition: Use published result datasets/appendices and model-run metadata from the official research release. Preserve task suite, elicitation and scaffold.
future_sources.likely_findings: 50%-success task time horizon, long-horizon autonomy curves, task duration, run cost/token use where disclosed, and scaffold sensitivity.
future_sources.value: Adds a different notion of capability: how long a task an agent can reliably complete, rather than one-shot benchmark accuracy.
